Interpretation
  • Every layer reproduces the pathologist well: AUC mRNA 0.952, miRNA 0.942, protein 0.931, all three 0.955. Here the label is not derived from any of the layers, so this is a fairer test of what the omics data know.
  • Why not AUC = 1? Look at the confident disagreements (6 of 198 test tumours). Four were called ER-negative by IHC yet have high ESR1 mRNA (three of them also high ER-α protein); two were called ER-positive although their ESR1 mRNA and ER-α protein are near zero (one of them is PAM50 Basal-like). Either the slide staining was borderline (ER positivity starts at only 1 % of stained cells), the tissue piece used for sequencing differed from the piece on the slide, or a labelling slip occurred. Labels have errors too – a model can never be more accurate than its reference, and its "mistakes" are sometimes the most interesting cases to re-check.

Step 7 · Pitfall: data leakage produces fake accuracy

Imagine a small study: 100 tumours and all ~13,500 genes. We shuffle the labels, so there is nothing to learn – the honest answer is chance (0.25).

  • Wrong way: pick the 20 "best" genes using all samples, then cross-validate.
  • Right way: put the gene selection inside the pipeline, so it is redone without the held-out fold each time.
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
small = rng.choice(y.index, size=100, replace=False)
X_small = layers['mRNA'].loc[small]                                    # 100 tumours x all genes
y_fake = pd.Series(rng.permutation(y[small].values), index=small)     # labels shuffled = pure noise

# WRONG: feature selection sees every sample, including the ones later used for testing
chosen = SelectKBest(f_classif, k=20).fit(X_small, y_fake).get_support()
wrong = cross_val_score(make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000)),
                        X_small.loc[:, chosen], y_fake, cv=cv, scoring='balanced_accuracy')

# RIGHT: selection is part of the pipeline, so it is repeated inside each training fold
right = cross_val_score(make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), SelectKBest(f_classif, k=20), LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000)),
                        X_small, y_fake, cv=cv, scoring='balanced_accuracy')
print(f'Shuffled labels - WRONG way: {wrong.mean():.2f}   RIGHT way: {right.mean():.2f}   (chance = 0.25)')
Output
Shuffled labels - WRONG way: 0.54   RIGHT way: 0.24   (chance = 0.25)
Interpretation

With labels that are pure noise, the wrong procedure reports a balanced accuracy of 0.54 – it looks like a publishable biomarker – while the correct procedure gives 0.24, i.e. chance. With 13,500 genes and only 100 samples, some genes match any labelling by luck; choosing them with the test samples in view smuggles the answer into the model. This mistake appears in published omics papers. Rule: every step that looks at the labels (feature selection, tuning) must happen inside cross-validation, and the test set is touched once.

Step 8 · Bonus: predict the subtype of tumours that have no label

Some tumours had no PAM50 call in the source data. We train the all-layers logistic regression on all labelled tumours and predict them. The predicted probability tells us how sure the model is.

final_model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), SelectKBest(f_classif, k=200), LogisticRegression(C=0.05, max_iter=5000))
final_model.fit(X_sets['All three'].loc[y.index], y)

proba = pd.DataFrame(final_model.predict_proba(X_sets['All three'].loc[unlabelled]),
                     index=unlabelled, columns=final_model.classes_)
predicted = proba.idxmax(axis=1)
confidence = proba.max(axis=1)
out = pd.DataFrame({'predicted_subtype': predicted, 'probability': confidence.round(3)})
out.to_csv(f'{ROOT}/results/tables/predicted_subtype_unlabelled.csv')
print('Predicted subtypes:', predicted.value_counts().to_dict())
print('Predictions with probability > 0.8:', (confidence > 0.8).sum(), 'of', len(confidence))
print('ER-IHC agreement: predicted Basal & ER-negative:',
      ((predicted == 'Basal') & (samples.loc[unlabelled, 'ER_status_IHC'] == 'Negative')).sum(),
      'of', (predicted == 'Basal').sum(), 'predicted Basal')
Output
Predicted subtypes: {'LumA': 111, 'Basal': 37, 'LumB': 20, 'Her2': 15}
Predictions with probability > 0.8: 158 of 183
ER-IHC agreement: predicted Basal & ER-negative: 28 of 37 predicted Basal
Interpretation
  • The 183 unlabelled tumours are predicted as LumA 111, Basal 37, LumB 20, Her2 15; 158 predictions have probability > 0.8. As in the labelled cohort, LumA is the largest group, but there are fewer LumB and relatively more Basal calls. Borderline LumB tumours may be called LumA, and the group without labels need not be a random sample – one more reason to treat these as predictions to check, not facts.
  • A quick sanity check with independent data: of the tumours predicted Basal-like, 28 of 37 are ER-negative by IHC – exactly what Basal-like biology predicts.
  • These are predictions, not diagnoses: low-probability calls should be reported as uncertain, and any clinical use would need validation on a new, independent cohort.

Take-home messages

  1. QC first: flag, decide, log. One bad “normal” sample changed the pair count.
  2. Bulk = mixture: many differentially expressed genes reflect cell composition (fat, blood).
  3. Significant ≠ important: report the FDR and the fold change; check with a count model.
  4. The layers agree on structure (subtypes), but mRNA is an imperfect proxy for protein.
  5. Correlation ≠ mechanism (miR-155 and SOCS1).
  6. Integration helps only when the layers carry complementary information.
  7. Check label circularity and use independent labels.
  8. Leakage turns noise into “biomarkers”.

Limitations and what professionals do next

Simplifications in this capstone
  • the main analysis is a t-test on log-CPM; PyDESeq2 is used as a check, without fold-change shrinkage
  • median imputation for missing protein values
  • early integration only
  • one cohort, no external validation
  • no correction for tumour purity
Next steps
  • a second count model (edgeR or limma-voom) and fold-change shrinkage
  • gene-set enrichment (GSEA, MSigDB, Reactome)
  • cell-type deconvolution (estimate purity and immune content)
  • MOFA / DIABLO integration
  • validation on METABRIC or another cohort
